question.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+8y=12{e}^{-2x}
$$

has the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)={e}^{-2x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡2x),$ find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

current_example.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d} x^2} + \frac{\textrm{d} y}{\textrm{d} x} - 2y = 20 e ^ {3x}.
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we find the complementary solution by solving the associated homogeneous ODE. Since the roots of the characteristic equation are $\lambda = 1, -2,$ we get

$$
y_c  = Ae^{x} + Be^{- 2 x}.
$$

Second, we find a particular solution of the inhomogeneous ODE. We see that the right-hand side is $20e^{3x},$ and $e^{3x}$ is not a term in the complementary solution, so we assume that a particular solution takes the form 

$$
y_p = \alpha e^{3x},
$$

where $\alpha$ is a constant to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of $y_p,$ we get

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}y_p}{\textrm{d}x} = 3 \alpha e ^{3x},
\quad \frac{\textrm{d}^2y_p}{\textrm{d}x^2} = 9  \alpha e ^{3x}.
$$

To find the value of $\alpha,$  we substitute the derivatives into the original ODE and get

$$
\begin{aligned}9\alpha {e}^{3x}+3\alpha {e}^{3x}-2\alpha {e}^{3x} & =20{e}^{3x} \\ \alpha (9+3-2){e}^{3x} & =20{e}^{3x} \\ 10\alpha {e}^{3x} & =20{e}^{3x} \\ 10\alpha  & =20 \\ \alpha  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particular solution is 

$$
y_p = 2e^{3x}
$$

and the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={y}_{c}+{y}_{p} \\  & =A{e}^{x}+B{e}^{-2x}+2{e}^{3x}.\end{aligned}
$$
